question: T12 (task-cbda50df28b03b07): in the phone view, as CAP-T12FALLZERO on the desktop: when a Wave Intensity fall takes the first Text block onto the Scrolling block's foot, does a second Text block under it go up by the first's move or by the foot's? On Blocks Probe at a 1600 by 1000 window, one new section per plan with a new Scrolling block and two Text blocks added after it, made on the desktop (desktop 1/2/3/26, 1/2/3/10 and 1/2/3/10; phone 1/2/3/10, 3/2/5/10 and 5/2/7/10). Then Mobile View (the frame 428 wide) and the plan's arranging there: 'arr' is arrow keys on the selected block, 'place i r0/c0/r1/c1' moves and resizes block i by hand. Y1: the first Text block one row up (ArrowUp, 2/2/4/10), then select the Scrolling block, Edit, Design ('open'), presses on Wave Intensity 150 and 0. Y2: the first Text block onto the top row (two ArrowUp) and made 1/2/3/6, the second placed at 5/2/7/6 and then 5/6/7/10 (in other columns than the first); 150 and 0. Y3: Y1's layout; presses 90, 180 (the range's end) and 0. Y4: Y1's layout; 90, then a real drag through one DevTools session pressed on 90, moved to 120, 150 and 180 and then to 0 in one move, 300 ms apart, a quick read 80 ms after each move and 80 and 1800 ms after the let go. Then Escape and a press on the page ('go'), Cmd+Z until as built, and Desktop View. R1 and R2 are two sessions (probe-y.mjs in the lane folder), each ran Y1 to Y4 with other plans of other tasks. Exit without saving each time.
readsAre: As CAP-T12DRAGFALL: layout of the Scrolling block and every block in its section (me: the Scrolling block; line: its drawing's height; sel: selected; kind; desktop and phone areas, top in the section and height), the section rows in the view shown, the Scrolling block's height, line (marquee and svg: top in the block and height), Undo and Redo, the panel's ranges; 'wave' is the panel's Wave Intensity value. 'inputs' holds each drag's quick reads (states: [name, { t: the page's clock, L: the layout as in reads, st: value, focus (isRange: the range has it), Undo/Redo, selected blocks, lines }]) and its events by the page's clock from the first (log: type, ms, the range's value). The read's name is the run, the plan, and the steps in order, '>' between them ('Z' is Cmd+Z, skipped when the section is back as built).
answer: Y1: 150 takes the Scrolling block to 1/2/7/10 and the Text blocks to 6/2/8/10 and 9/2/11/10 (10 rows). 0 takes the Scrolling block to 1/2/2/10 and the first Text block onto the foot at 2/2/4/10 (4 rows up), and the second goes up by the same 4 rows to 5/2/7/10, not by the foot's 5 (4/2/6/10); 6 rows.

Y2, the second Text block in other columns: 150 takes them from 1/2/3/6 and 5/6/7/10 to 5/2/7/6 and 9/6/11/10 (10 rows); 0 takes the first onto the foot at 2/2/4/6 (3 rows up) and the second to 6/6/8/10, 3 rows up, not 5 (4/6/6/10); 7 rows. It shares no column with the first.

Y3: 90 takes them to 1/2/5/10, 4/2/6/10 and 7/2/9/10 (8 rows); 180 to 1/2/8/10, 7/2/9/10 and 10/2/12/10 (11 rows); 0 to 1/2/2/10, 2/2/4/10 and 5/2/7/10, both 5 rows up, not the foot's 6; 6 rows. Y4: 80 ms after each move the drag shows 1/2/6/10, 1/2/7/10 and 1/2/8/10 at 120, 150 and 180 (the Text blocks 5/2/7/10 and 8/2/10/10 to 7/2/9/10 and 10/2/12/10), and the jump 180 to 0 gives Y3's 0 at once; the let go keeps it.

So the phone view takes the desktop's rule: when a fall would take one block onto the Scrolling block's top row or above, it lands on the foot and every other block that follows goes up by its move. The desktop areas stay as made throughout.

Escape keeps every area; each press, and the drag, is one undo step: Cmd+Z gives back the steps one by one, then the arranging. R1 and R2 read alike in every read and every quick read (areas, rows, line, Undo and Redo, the value), Redo at a plan's start apart (it stays on from the plan before).
Not read: two blocks that would land on the foot from different rows; a phone fall by Text Size.
